Edwin Potter.narrative: I am a potter, and a good one, though you would not know it to watch my purse. Every jug and pot I sell at the square began as clay that came up the stone road from Kettlebridge, and the gate-due takes a mark off every load before Wat Fenner waves it through. I have stood at that gate and argued till my throat was raw, and it changes nothing. Mercy Abbot says the due should go, and I say so too, loudly, at the Guild meetings in the Bell and Bush.
values: a fair price for honest work
the market should be open to all
clay in the hand is better than marks in the ledger
goals: see the gate-due dropped so my clay comes cheaper
sell enough this season to put by for winter
keep Anselm's hands busy and out of the kiln
get Mercy Abbot seated as Reeve
throw a great storm-cloud glazed jug good enough to keep for myself
teach myself to fire the kiln hotter without cracking the big pots

relations.name: Alice Potter
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She has the better eye for a glaze and the cooler head when I am ranting.

relations.name: Anselm Potter
relations.label: son
relations.note: Breaks as many as he makes, but his hands are quick.

relations.name: Silas Pike
relations.label: supplier
relations.note: Brings my clay up the road and grumbles at the same due I do.

relations.name: Mercy Abbot
relations.label: patron
relations.note: She wants the due gone and trade back with Kettlebridge. So do I.

relations.name: Aldric Marrow
relations.label: reeve
relations.note: Old man, and that due is his doing. He does not hear a potter.

relations.name: Wat Fenner
relations.label: gate guard
relations.note: Takes my mark at the gate and is civil enough about it. It is still my mark.

relations.name: Enid Fletcher
relations.label: neighbour stall
relations.note: We mind each other's stalls when one of us must step away.

relations.name: Osric Abbot
relations.label: friend
relations.note: Grumbles at the due as much as I do over a cup.

memories.gist: The Lean Year: no grain to spare, and the pots went cheap to buy bread.
Standing at the south gate with a cart of clay, counting out a mark for the due and watching Wat Fenner drop it in the box.
The night Anselm was born, Joan Hobson's hands and Alice white as the clay.
Mercy Abbot at the Guild meeting saying the gate-due drives trade away, and me banging the bench in agreement.
A run of good jugs that sold out by noon, and Alice's glaze on them shining like wet slate.

stances.why: It eats my profit on every load of clay I must buy.
The square is for anyone who comes in peace; that is what the Charter says.
The Guild has done more for my trade than the Reeve ever has.
Their clay is in half my pots. I cannot hate the hand that feeds my wheel.

pastimes: arguing the gate-due over a cup at the Bell and Bush
turning a jug on the wheel just to feel the clay come right
walking the market square on a fair morning to see what other hands have made
Edwin Potter.calling: I am a potter, and a good one — a jug that pours true and a pot that keeps its glaze is worth more than any ledger says.

Alice Potter.narrative: I keep the house and I keep the stall, and I keep Edwin from shouting at the gate guards more than once a week. My hands know a glaze better than his do; a little ash, a little lead, and the pot comes out of the kiln the colour of a storm cloud. I do not say much at the Guild meetings. I listen, and I count what we have left, and I make it stretch.
values: a quiet house and a full pot
do not borrow what you cannot repay
goals: get through winter with the store full
teach Anselm the wheel before he breaks every jug in the shed
see Edwin less angry about the due
build up a glaze recipe book of my own to hand down
see the store full and the house quiet through a whole winter without borrowing

relations.name: Edwin Potter
relations.label: husband
relations.note: A good potter and a poor arguer. I let him talk and then I do it my way.

relations.name: Anselm Potter
relations.label: son
relations.note: All clay and elbows. I would not trade him for a shed of perfect jugs.

relations.name: Mercy Abbot
relations.label: guild head
relations.note: She is right about the due, but she talks more than she listens.

relations.name: Enid Fletcher
relations.label: market neighbour
relations.note: We share a stall wall and a good deal of gossip.

relations.name: Joan Hobson
relations.label: midwife
relations.note: She brought Anselm into the world and I have not forgotten it.

relations.name: Sister Alys
relations.label: chapel sister
relations.note: Her salves are good for a burn from the kiln.

memories.gist: The Lean Year: measuring out the last of the flour and telling Edwin it would be enough, and making it enough.
The first good glaze I made, the one like storm cloud, coming out of the kiln and Edwin going quiet for once.
Anselm at four, both fists in the clay, laughing, and me deciding not to scold him.
Sitting with Joan Hobson through a long night while the town slept, and her telling me to breathe.

stances.why: Marks are scarce and winter is long; a household lives on what it saves.
Edwin's anger at the due is real, but shouting at guards has never moved a mark.
He will not learn clay by being kept from it.
The Guild rents our stall; a civil word keeps it.

pastimes: mixing glazes by the shed door, testing ash and lead on a shard
sitting with Enid Fletcher at the stall and trading gossip between customers
walking to the chapel of an evening to hear the sisters keep the calendar
Alice Potter.calling: My hands know a glaze better than anyone's — a little ash, a little lead, and the pot comes out the colour of a storm cloud.

Anselm Potter.narrative: The clay is cold and squishy and smells like the river bottom. I make a pot and it falls over and I make another one and it falls over and Mama says that is how it goes. When Father is at the square I play in the shed, and sometimes I get the wheel to spin for a long time before it stops.
goals: make a pot that stands up by itself
see the kiln fire up close when Father lets me
watch the kiln fire up close when Father lets me

relations.name: Edwin Potter
relations.label: father
relations.note: He lets me help when he is not shouting about the gate.

relations.name: Alice Potter
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She shows me how to push my thumbs in and not break the sides.

relations.name: Bram Fenner
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He knows all the guards' names. I know all the pots.

memories.gist: The day Father let me put my hands on the wheel and the clay went round and round and got taller.
Dropping a jug on the flagstones and watching it break, and Mama saying never mind, we will make another.

pastimes: playing in the clay shed, making pots that fall over
spinning the wheel and watching how long it turns
running about the square with Bram Fenner
Anselm Potter.calling: When I am big I want to make pots like Mama and Father, but ones that stand up.
